messages:
alex: quick q — if a request matches both a header anchor and a cookie anchor which one should the matcher prefer? example: path=/checkout, header: X-Region=eu, cookie: ab_test=variantB. console today highlights header hints but cookies are invisible. this matters for canaries + quotas
priya: do we have a current formal priority list? i thought anchors were scored by specificity then tiebroken by anchor type
danny: runtime today scores anchors then picks highest score. anchor types have implicit weights: host(100), path(90), header(70), query(50), cookie(40). that comes from old heuristics. not strongly documented though
tess: fwiw i think header > cookie makes sense: headers are explicit per-request, cookies can be stale or user-manipulated. but for session-affinity (sticky sessions) cookie should be able to override path for that user
alex: agreed on session-affinity. but we need consistent quota assignment. if cookie wins sometimes and header other times we might split usage across routes and break per-route quotas
danny: right. two problems: 1) quota keys (billing/ratelimit) need a deterministic mapping from request -> matched route; 2) console UX needs to show why a route was chosen (which anchors matched)
priya: proposal: make priority deterministic and simple: 1) host 2) path 3) header 4) query 5) cookie, but add a per-route flag `session_affinity_cookie` that, when enabled, elevates cookie to just above path for that specific route. also emit telemetry tag `anchor_winner` and `anchor_stack` for explainability
routebot: config: runtime.match.priority=["host","path","header","query","cookie"] (can be overridden per-tenant)
danny: i like the per-route override, but needs guardrails. if cookie can be promoted, we should require a TTL and an origin verification (signed cookie) to avoid gaming quotas. otherwise customers could set cookies to steer traffic into cheaper routes
tess: console change: add inline explain pill on route line: "matched by header X-Region:eu" or "matched by cookie ab_test=variantB (affinity)". also show which anchor lost (e.g., header won over cookie)
alex: telemetry: please make sure we can reconstruct the decision tree: anchor_stack should be ordered list of anchors that matched with scores, anchor_winner single string. will also need a metric: "anchor_override_rate" per route to detect weird behavior
priya: for quotas i propose using the final resolved route id as the quota key unless `affinity_override=true` and signed_cookie=true, in which case we use signed_cookie.value as session key prefix + route id. defaults avoid cookie-based quota keys
danny: one more nuance: query param anchors are often used for embed tokens. should they be higher than cookies? currently we rank query > cookie but maybe query should be lower because ephemeral tokens are less stable. open to data here
tess: small implementation detail: matcher should produce a stable canonicalization of cookie values (truncate/prefix) when used in telemetry so we don't leak PII
alex: next steps: priya/eng-ux will draft console hint copy + telemetry fields. danny/eng-runtime will add deterministic priority list + per-route cookie elevation with signed-cookie requirement. i'll file a short RFC and test matrix. :thumbsup:
priya: i'll add the console mock and the telemetry schema. tagging @tess for the pill design
danny: i'll add unit tests covering: cookie promoted, cookie rejected (unsigned), header wins, quota-key generation. also add a small perf check for anchor_stack emission overhead
routebot: deploy plan: rollout match.priority change as a config flag in staged rollout to 20% tenants, monitor anchor_override_rate and quota divergence metric
alex: perfect. thanks everyone.
